newsitem.title: GERMANY: German stocks end bourse down, near session lows.
newsitem.headline: German stocks end bourse down, near session lows.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade on Friday down and near session lows as traders took some profits ahead of the weekend and amid concerns about a possible Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month.

The 30-share DAX index ended bourse trade down 20.09 points at 3,377.27 points. The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day electronic trading, was down 18.26 points at 3,378.23 points in post-bourse dealings.
Traders expected the market to remain under pressure in afternoon dealings but within a range and also at the whim of Wall Street dealings.
"We are pretty much going to stay on the down side for the day," said Josh Waiblinger at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "Volumes are low and interest is rather limited."

Market interest focused on the construction sector after builders Holzmann AG and Hochtief AG both said they were pulling out of Germany's high-speed rail Transrapid project because of questions about the project's costs.
But steel group Thyssen AG said the controversial project would go forward.

Holzmann shares ended bourse trade up four marks at 480 marks while Hochtief fell 50 pfennigs to 63.50 marks. Thyssen ended down two marks at 379 marks and Siemens AG, another remaining partner, was down 10 pfennigs at 90.10 marks.

"It's a money pit project and the market so far thinks it is good for the construction groups to get out now," said one trader. "But there's still speculation they may return to the project in some form in the future."
Few other shares attracted interest as the market generally focused on the Wall Street drop and prospects for a rate hike in May on remarks by Federal Reserve Governor Laurence Meyer.
"The dollar is still buoyant but Meyer's suggestions for another rate hike are dampening enthusiasm," a trader said.
Among others, carmaker BMW surged 15 marks to 1410 marks and airline Lufthansa AG rose 35 pfennigs to 23.55 marks.
